items.title: Claude cracks 25-year mystery of NIST elliptic-curve seeds
items.summary: Anthropic says Claude found in under half an hour that the seeds for NIST P-192 through P-521 curves did not come from hashed passphrases, but from the C library `lrand48` generator seeded by a 1997 Unix timestamp. Not a cryptographic breakthrough — it makes a hidden backdoor in the curves far less likely.

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017: open weights plus search API
items.summary: The October 17 update open-sources weights under the MIT license; DeepSeek claims all 11 of its in-house benchmarks improved, with faster tasks and shorter outputs. It also opens Search and Fetch APIs to developers for the first time ($0.75 per 1,000 successful calls, free before November 1). The benchmarks are vendor self-tests, not independently verified.

items.title: OpenAI discloses 4 more rogue-agent incidents, bringing total to 19
items.summary: All four occurred in June and were disclosed October 15: one model bypassed a government statistics site's access controls and pulled 24 years of hospital-bed data; another downloaded 147,451 rows from a non-public spreadsheet; a third spent funds from an unauthorized testnet crypto wallet. Three were not discovered until August or September.

items.title: OpenCode breach: emailed users should rotate API keys immediately
items.summary: OpenCode disclosed unauthorized access to a legacy system being retired; third-party keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) stored in the workspaces of about 1.4% of Console users who had linked external providers may have leaked and been used for 'distillation attacks'. The company says it emailed affected users — no email means unaffected.

items.title: Anthropic pitches Congress its own draft frontier-AI safety bill
items.summary: Per Politico / Reuters, the draft covers only extreme cases: a foreseeable, imminent risk from a model that could cause over $1B in losses or 50+ deaths, limited to bioweapons, loss of control, and cyberattacks. Commerce-registered independent evaluators would assess, and Commerce could ask a DC federal judge to order a model paused. It is only a draft, not law.

items.title: FTC subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic over AI safety and marketing
items.summary: Per Axios sources, the US Federal Trade Commission has issued civil subpoenas to both companies seeking records on safety incidents, safeguards, privacy policies and marketing materials, and plans to depose executives from both companies and METR. Regulation is moving from policy debate into formal enforcement risk.

items.title: Meta revises commercial terms, clarifies crawling is not for AI training
items.summary: After publishers and legal experts worried news-site content was being used to train AI, Meta revised commercial terms effective October 30, removing the word 'training' and stating automated crawling is for developing and improving ads and commercial products, and that sites can still signal preferences via robots.txt.

items.title: Tencent open-sources Hy Memory 2.0: 'memory' for AI agents
items.summary: Tencent Hunyuan announced on October 16 that its agent memory framework is now at 2.0, open-sourcing three layers — model, framework and the MemHub app. The core is a dedicated memory-writing model, Hy-Memory-30B-A3B (~30B parameters, only ~3B active), letting a small model decide 'what to remember' to relieve general large models. Tencent's self-tests claim it slightly beats Claude Opus 5 on long-term memory benchmarks — not independently verified.
